name: Paul Irish
category: Front-end tooling engineer (HTML5 Boilerplate, Chrome DevTools)
milestone_by_age_26: HTML5 Boilerplate launched August 2010 and Modernizr/Chrome DevTools prominence are ~age 27–28+ if born ~1982; no clearly dated material personal OSS/product breakout at or before age 26 found in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Paul Irish's defining public milestones (HTML5 Boilerplate 2010 with Divya Manian; Modernizr; Chrome DevTools advocacy) land after age 26 under the ~1982 birth-year assumption. Birth date itself is weakly documented; eligibility fails on milestone timing.

name: Jake Archibald
milestone_by_age_26: Chrome engineering leadership and Service Worker advocacy/fame are mid-career; no specific independently dated material personal product/framework/founder milestone by age 26 found in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Known for Google Chrome web-platform work and developer advocacy; reviewed sources do not establish a dated personal breakout at or before age 26.

name: Rich Harris
milestone_by_age_26: Created Ractive.js in 2013 (predecessor to Svelte) while building interactive journalism tooling, at about age 26 under the ~1987 cohort birth year; Svelte v1 followed in 2016.
early_history_summary: British interactive journalist/graphics developer who built UI tooling to ship data-rich stories at places including Citywire and The Guardian. Created Ractive.js (2013) for reactive interfaces, then evolved that compiler-oriented approach into Svelte (2016) and also created Rollup.
primary_early_advantage_tags: interactive journalism, Ractive, Guardian graphics, Svelte compiler model
evidence_summary: Ractive (2013) is the age-26-or-under milestone enabling later Svelte. Domain immersion in newsroom interactives drove framework design more than documented inherited capital. Exact birth date is less solid than project dates; age uses cohort birth_year 1987.
starting_point: British journalism-to-engineering path; early career as financial/video journalist and web producer before Guardian interactive work (family details not documented).
current_position: Svelte maintainer working on Svelte at Vercel; creator of Svelte, Ractive, and Rollup; former NYT graphics editor.

trajectory.event: Created Ractive.js for reactive interactive journalism UIs.
Created Rollup, a next-generation JavaScript module bundler.
Released Svelte 1.0 as a compile-time UI framework evolving from Ractive ideas.
Svelte 3 reimagined reactivity with widespread community adoption.
Joined Vercel to work full-time on Svelte/SvelteKit.

name: Taylor Otwell
milestone_by_age_26: Created and released Laravel in 2011 as a side project (~age 25) after IT degree work and dissatisfaction with CodeIgniter; framework became the dominant modern PHP stack.
early_history_summary: Arkansas-based developer; Information Technology bachelor's (Arkansas Tech, ~2004–2008). Built Laravel nights/weekends while employed, drawing on ASP.NET experience to improve PHP ergonomics (DI, ORM, templating). Later commercialized surrounding products (Forge, etc.) and took Laravel full-time.
family_context_summary: Based in Arkansas; detailed parental professions/wealth not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Laravel side project, PHP ecosystem, open-source distribution, Arkansas solo founder
evidence_summary: Laravel 2011 release at ~25 is a clear material milestone, later compounded by Forge and commercial products. Advantage stack is skill plus open-source distribution rather than elite coastal network or documented family capital. A contemporary interview calling himself a 26-year-old developer and 2004–2008 degree timeline support ~1986 birth cohort.
starting_point: Arkansas, US; IT degree path into PHP development and solo open-source framework creation.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Laravel; leads Laravel framework and commercial cloud/tooling products from a bootstrapped-to-scaled open-source business.

trajectory.event: Completed Information Technology bachelor's degree path (~Arkansas Tech).
Released Laravel PHP framework as a personal side project.
Launched Laravel Forge and found early product-market fit for paid hosting automation.
Went full-time on Laravel ecosystem after years of dual employment/side-project work.
Continued expanding Laravel Cloud and commercial products while remaining framework lead.

name: Adam Wathan
milestone_by_age_26: First book and full-time indie transition in 2016 (~age 27); Tailwind CSS public traction ~2017–2019 at ages 28–30+. No material by-26 product breakout documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Adam's own site dates full-time indie shift to 2016 book launch; Tailwind is later. Under ~1989 birth year, both are post-26.

name: Fabien Potencier
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Sensio (later SensioLabs) in Paris in 1998 right after studies (~age 19) and founded the Symfony project in 2004 (~age 25), open-sourcing a major PHP framework.
early_history_summary: French entrepreneur/engineer who co-founded web agency Sensio with Grégory Pascal in 1998 after finishing studies, then extracted and open-sourced Symfony to productize best practices for PHP web apps. Long-term project lead of Symfony and serial SensioLabs entrepreneur.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sensio cofounder, PHP agency work, Symfony open source, Paris tech
evidence_summary: Sensio founding (1998) and Symfony project founding (2004) both fall at or before 26 under the 1979 birth-year assumption used in candidate metadata and career timelines. Cofounder partnership and customer-driven framework design are clearer than family capital documentation.
starting_point: France; finished studies late 1990s and immediately co-founded Sensio web company in Paris.
current_position: Symfony founder/project lead and long-time SensioLabs/Upsun operator-executive in the PHP ecosystem.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Sensio (later SensioLabs) in Paris with Grégory Pascal after studies.
Founded the Symfony project to codify PHP web application best practices.
Open-sourced Symfony, beginning two decades of framework leadership.
Symfony celebrated five years as a major open-source PHP framework.
Sensio rebranded/expanded as SensioLabs commercial open-source company.

name: Graydon Hoare
milestone_by_age_26: Started Rust as a personal project in 2006 at about age 29 while at Mozilla (MIT Technology Review: 29-year-old in 2006). No material public language/product breakout by age 26 found in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Rust origin is firmly dated to 2006 at age ~29; Mozilla sponsorship 2009 and Rust 1.0 in 2015 are later. Ineligible under age-26 rule despite legendary later impact.

name: Andrew Kelley
milestone_by_age_26: Started designing and announcing the Zig programming language in 2015 at about age 25 as a systems language alternative to C with explicit control-flow and allocation principles.
early_history_summary: Systems programmer who began Zig while ostensibly working on a digital audio workstation, turning language design into the primary project. Later left full-time employment (around 2018) to work on Zig and formed the Zig Software Foundation as president/lead developer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Zig 2015, systems programming, open-source language design, later ZSF
evidence_summary: Zig's 2015 start at ~age 25 is the by-26 milestone; later full-time open-source and foundation formalization compound it. Birth year relies on candidate metadata (~1990) aligned with 2015 start and 2018 full-time shift. Family advantages not documented.
starting_point: Not documented in detail; systems programmer who pivoted a side language experiment into Zig (family/class origin unclear in reviewed sources).
current_position: President and lead developer of the Zig Software Foundation; creator of the Zig programming language.

trajectory.event: Began designing and publicly introducing the Zig programming language.
Quit day job to work full-time on Zig open source.
Formalized Zig Software Foundation leadership and funding model.
Zig continued gaining production adoption in systems tooling communities (e.g., Ghostty, TigerBeetle ecosystem attention).

name: Russ Cox
milestone_by_age_26: Influential Go compiler/runtime leadership began when joining the Go team around 2008 (~age 30). High-school/college Bell Labs proximity is notable pipeline access but not a public personal product milestone by 26; Plan 9-era student work is not a clear independent breakout under this rubric.
family_context_summary: Grew up near Bell Labs (family/geo proximity). Detailed finances not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented beyond regional proximity to Bell Labs research culture.
evidence_summary: Go fame and tech leadership are post-26. Early Bell Labs exposure is real but insufficient as a dated public milestone by age 26 under strict eligibility rules.

name: Salvatore Sanfilippo
milestone_by_age_26: Created and released hping, a widely used TCP/IP packet generator/analyzer for network security testing, around 1998 at about age 21 (born 7 March 1977); also invented the idle scan technique implemented by nmap.
early_history_summary: Born 7 March 1977 in Campobello di Licata, Sicily; moved to Palermo at 17 intending architecture studies then shifted to computing. Built security tools in the late 1990s (hping, idle scan). Later created Redis in 2009 (age 32), which became the globally dominant in-memory data structure server.
family_context_summary: Grew up in a marginalized area of southern Sicily near Gela; later moved to Palermo. Not a privileged documented capital path.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as computing-domain family transfer in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sicily outsider path, hping 1998, security tooling, later Redis
evidence_summary: hping (~1998, age 21) is a verified material security-tooling milestone well before 26; Redis (2009) is the larger later achievement at age 32. Constraint/outsider context is better documented than family capital.
starting_point: Born 7 March 1977 in Campobello di Licata, Sicily; raised near Gela then moved to Palermo at 17.
current_position: Redis creator (antirez); returned to Redis-related work after a multi-year break; Italian systems programmer and author based in Sicily.

trajectory.event: Released hping, a major open-source TCP/IP security testing utility.
Continued security tooling career while supporting a young family in Italy.
Created and announced Redis, which became a foundational in-memory data store.
Joined Redis Labs to lead open-source Redis development.
Stepped back from Redis leadership for family and other projects.
Returned to Redis with a public welcome-back from the company.

name: Hadley Wickham
milestone_by_age_26: Awarded the John Chambers Award for Statistical Computing in 2006 at age 26 for tools for data reshaping and visualisation (early reshape/ggplot ecosystem work during PhD training).
early_history_summary: Born 14 October 1979 in Hamilton, New Zealand. Studied human biology and statistics at University of Auckland (BSc/MSc), then PhD at Iowa State (2008) under Di Cook and Heike Hofmann. Built the reshape/ggplot lineage of tools that became ggplot2 and later the tidyverse as Posit (RStudio) chief scientist.
family_context_summary: New Zealand upbringing; sister Charlotte Wickham also became a statistician/data scientist educator.
parent_family_domain_summary: Sibling later also in statistics; parental professions not detailed in reviewed sources. Some talks reference teenage spreadsheets/databases for father's job context.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Iowa State PhD, Di Cook/Heike Hofmann, Chambers Award, R graphics ecosystem
evidence_summary: Chambers Award 2006 at age 26 certifies material early contribution to statistical computing tools. Auckland + Iowa State pipeline and visualization mentors matter; ggplot2 book (2009) and tidyverse branding are later amplifications.
starting_point: Born 14 October 1979 in Hamilton, New Zealand; Auckland statistics training then US PhD path.
current_position: Chief Scientist at Posit (formerly RStudio); leader of the tidyverse; adjunct professor affiliations; COPSS Presidents' Award winner (2019).

trajectory.event: Completed Auckland degrees and moved into advanced statistics training toward Iowa State PhD.
Received John Chambers Award for Statistical Computing for reshaping/visualization tools.
Finished PhD Practical tools for exploring data and models at Iowa State.
Published ggplot2 book, cementing Grammar of Graphics tooling in R.
Named ASA Fellow for statistical graphics and computing contributions.
Won COPSS Presidents' Award for accessible statistical computing and visualization.

name: Wes McKinney
milestone_by_age_26: Open-sourced pandas in 2009 at about age 24 while working in quant finance at AQR Capital Management after graduating MIT in 2007.
early_history_summary: MIT pure math BS (2007), then AQR Capital (2007–2010) where he learned Python and built pandas for financial data workflows. Open-sourced pandas in 2009; later left Duke Statistics PhD (started 2010) to work full-time on pandas and wrote Python for Data Analysis; went on to Apache Arrow, Datapad, Ursa Labs/Voltron Data, and Posit.
family_context_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources; MIT + finance job provided runway to experiment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT math, AQR finance domain, pandas 2009, Python data wave
evidence_summary: pandas public release in 2009 at ~24 is a clear material milestone, with MIT education and quant-finance problem immersion as primary early advantages. Later Arrow/Voltron work is post-26 amplification. Birth year ~1985 inferred from MIT 2007 graduation and self-reported ages in talks (~23 in 2008, ~26 when full-time on pandas ~2011).
starting_point: US; MIT pure mathematics graduate (2007) entering quant finance at AQR during the financial crisis.
current_position: Principal Architect at Posit; creator of pandas and Apache Arrow co-creator; former Datapad/Ursa Labs/Voltron Data founder-executive.

trajectory.event: Graduated MIT with BS in Mathematics and joined AQR Capital Management.
Open-sourced pandas, created for financial data analysis workflows at AQR.
Left Duke Statistics PhD path to work full-time on pandas.
Published Python for Data Analysis and co-founded Lambda Foundry.
Co-founded Datapad (acquired by Cloudera in 2014).
Launched Ursa Labs to advance Apache Arrow open-source data infrastructure.
